jobs.description: About us At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too. The role Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer. You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients. You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job. Key responsibilities Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list. Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them. Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs. Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses. Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path. Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended. Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client. Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse. Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards. Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need. Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait. Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live. jobs.description: Operations & Strategy Manager Permanent employee · Full-time · Berlin (HQ) Our mission for you European energy costs are twice as high as in the US and China, and electricity demand is expected to double by 2050. This puts European industry under massive cost pressure – and companies need to act now. trawa is building the solution: the first integrated B2B energy platform that brings together energy procurement, energy management and the marketing of flexible assets in one product. This helps companies save up to 30% on their recurring electricity costs while switching to renewable energy. We're the fastest-growing B2B energy platform in Europe. Active in Germany and Austria now, and expanding operations to a third market in 2027. We're on the road to European scale and move fast – the market window is open and we intend to own it. Now we are looking for an Operations & Strategy Manager to own a business-critical part of our energy value chain: the processes behind how we configure, price and quote long-term energy products for our customers. About trawa trawa is a tech-driven scale-up based in Berlin with around 100 employees, combining deep energy market expertise with in-house software development. We've raised over €35M to date, most recently a €24M Series A in May 2025, backed by Balderton, Headline, Speedinvest, AENU, Magnetic and Tiny VC. This role is based in our Berlin office, where we work together in person most of the week. We offer flexible working hours, so you can shape your day in a way that works for you. The Team You'll join our Energy & Trading team, which owns the energy side of our business – from sourcing and portfolio management to making sure our customers' energy products work in practice. You'll report directly to our Energy & Trading Manager and work closely with the COO, our Trading Team, Sales, Pricing, Product and Tech. You start without direct reports, but with a clear mandate: own our CPQ process end-to-end and grow the margin it generates. Who we are looking for Strong quantitative skills: You think analytically, feel at home with numbers and data and can confidently challenge quantitative results – without having to be a quant or developer yourself. Ideally, you have a degree in a quantitative or business field (e.g. economics, engineering, industrial engineering, business administration). Business acumen & process mindset: You think commercially, care about margins and unit economics, enjoy turning messy processes into robust, scalable ones and prioritise by impact. Experience with commercial processes such as pricing or deal desks, in energy, financial services or any other industry, is a plus. Interest in energy markets: You are fascinated by how energy markets work – from wholesale and forward markets to PPAs, hedging and pricing – and want to dive deep into them. Knowledge of the German energy market is a plus; experience in (energy) trading is explicitly not required – what matters is your drive to understand the mechanics and make the processes behind them work. Hungry & ambitious: You want to grow fast, take on responsibility early and set high standards for yourself. You don't wait for instructions and enjoy a steep learning curve, and work experience in a high-paced environment, e.g. a start-up, scale-up or consulting, is a plus. High ownership & structured execution: You drive topics end-to-end, align stakeholders across departments and turn ideas into scalable processes with tangible business impact. An affinity for AI-powered tools and automation to make processes faster and smarter is a plus. Strong communication: You speak German at native level and very good English, and you translate confidently between commercial, quantitative and operational perspectives. jobs.description: Company Overview Mindpeak is a Hamburg-based AI company on a mission to make cancer diagnosis more accurate, efficient and personalized. We build deep-learning solutions for computational pathology that bring AI directly into clinical practice. Our technology is already used in routine diagnostics across more than 25 countries and supports leading pharmaceutical and biotech companies in developing and advancing new cancer treatments. What makes Mindpeak special is the combination of disciplines required to make this work. Software engineers and machine learning experts work alongside pathologists, scientists, product specialists and commercial teams to turn cutting-edge AI into products that deliver real value in healthcare. This also makes building our team unusually interesting. Many of the people we hire sit at the intersection of different disciplines and are difficult to find through conventional recruiting. Identifying exceptional talent, understanding what great looks like and building hiring processes that allow us to make consistently strong decisions are therefore critical to Mindpeak’s next stage of growth. The Role We are looking for a Senior Talent Acquisition Manager to take ownership of recruiting across Mindpeak. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who genuinely enjoys recruiting and sees Talent Acquisition itself as their profession. You will recruit across different functions, with a particular focus on senior, business-critical and hard-to-fill roles spanning Product, Technology and Business. You will work closely with our founders and hiring managers to define what we actually need, identify what great looks like for each role and translate this into rigorous, efficient hiring processes. This is a hands-on recruiting role, not a generalist People & Culture or Organizational Development position. At the same time, we expect you to help raise the quality of hiring across Mindpeak by challenging unclear requirements, improving interview practices and bringing structure and discipline to how we make hiring decisions. You will not inherit a recruiting team, but you will have the mandate and budget to work with external recruiters and specialist search partners where they add value. Select, brief and actively manage external recruiters and search partners where they add value. Keep pipelines, bottlenecks and risks transparent for leadership, and keep improving how Mindpeak hires without unnecessary bureaucracy. Interviews across Mindpeak become more rigorous and consistent , based on evidence rather than titles or impressions. Most importantly, critical roles get closed with people who raise the quality of the organisation. Your Experience Substantial hands-on experience owning full-cycle recruiting; a background in executive search or another environment with a strong sourcing and assessment culture is a plus. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Intern
jobs.description: About Andercore Andercore is the AI-native supplier of industrial materials and goods for energy and infrastructure. We execute trade and distribution end-to-end, on our own account, at the speed of compute - and we are becoming the supplier of record for the entire industry. Industrial procurement is a €900B market in Europe alone and the largest manual market on earth. 95% of customers have no direct access to global supply chains. Materials pass through four or five intermediaries before they reach a site, and 40% of the margin evaporates on the way. For decades, the operating system of this industry was people: people to source, negotiate, finance, ship, and sell. We built the alternative from scratch. We are the supplier. We buy from global sources and sell to European customers on our own account. Our AI runs the full trade: sourcing, quality, pricing, sales, logistics, credit, and financing. One request. A firm quote in minutes. Delivered on time. For the customer, it feels like buying from their preferred local supplier. No warehouses. No fleet. No inventory risk. Every trade is pre-sold before it is bought. We are also the credit counterparty. Customers are scored and insured in minutes and get up to 60 days of payment terms priced into the quote itself. The working capital behind every trade is bank-funded, not equity-funded. Where we are today: Strong triple-digit-million euro turnover run rate, the majority of it from repeat customers Seven European markets live, sourced from suppliers across Asia and beyond 80+ people across Berlin (HQ), London, and Shanghai $90M raised in equity and debt, including our $40M Series B, from Atomico, Project A, Target Global, and Inven Capital - with working capital facilities from UniCredit and KfW The margin is in the bits. The moat is in the atoms. We are building the supplier of record for industrial materials - and redefining how global trade works in one of the largest and most essential industries on earth. About the role Learn how a global trading business really works, and build the AI tools that make it faster. As a Forward Deployed Intern, you spend six months inside our business. You sit with the teams that buy, sell and move industrial materials, learn how their work really happens, and build tools that make it faster, with AI at the core. You work alongside our product and engineering team, with a mentor who reviews your work and helps you grow. This is not a shadowing internship: you take on real problems, ship real tools, and see them used every day. What you will do Learn the business Join our sales, procurement, logistics and finance teams and understand how a trade works from request to delivery. Spot where people lose time to manual work. Build , Measure & Share Build automations, small agents, scripts and dashboards with AI tools such as Claude. Ship first versions quickly and improve them with feedback from the people who use them. Track whether what you built saves time or prevents mistakes. Decide with your mentor what to improve and what to stop. Document what you built so others can use it. Show your work in demos to the team. What success looks like Several tools or automations in daily use by our teams Measured time savings for at least one team Clear documentation others can build on A solid understanding of how a global trade works end to end What you bring You are enrolled in a degree in computer science, engineering, business informatics or a similar field. You can code, for example in Python or JavaScript, and use AI tools in your daily work. Real curiosity about how businesses work, not only about technology. You communicate clearly and like working with people from other backgrounds. You can commit to six months full-time in Berlin. Fluent English. German is a plus. jobs.description: About Jimdo We exist to unleash the power of the self-employed - helping solopreneurs and micro-businesses thrive by doing what they're passionate about and removing the complexity of building lasting, successful businesses. Jimdo started in 2007 when three school friends built a website builder in a Northern German farmhouse to help everyone build a presence online. Today, we're a profitable, remote-first company with 220+ people from 50+ nationalities working across 15+ countries. We've helped build over 36 million websites to get online across the world. We're more than just a website builder. We're an AI-powered platform that helps self-employed people actually run and build successful businesses — from getting found online, winning customers and running their business with a peace of mind by knowing exactly what to do next to move forward. At the heart of Jimdo is a strong belief in personalized, data-driven guidance. Our platform combines design, business tools, and an AI-powered core that turns real customer data into clear insights and next steps helping our customers focus on what moves their business forward. Role Overview At Jimdo, we think the best support is the one a customer never needs. When our customers, self-employed people and small business owners, do need help, it should come fast: from self-service and AI first, and from a person when that's what the case needs. We're bringing our support tooling, Zendesk, chatbots and AI work together into one team with one backlog and one roadmap. As Senior Product Owner, you'll lead that team and own the outcome: more questions answered by AI, faster help, lower cost to serve, and customers who still trust us. You'll also shape where this goes next. Over the next couple of years AI will handle more and more first-line support, and you'll decide how the work is split between AI and people, and build the platform around it. The team and who you'll work with You'll report to the Head of Customer Support Services and join CSS, our support organisation. You'll lead a small team of Zendesk and AI specialists and work day to day with the engineers who build our support tools. You'll work closely with our knowledge and readiness team, support agents and team leads, product teams, our Company AI team, Data & Analytics, and our support and AI vendors. What you'll be doing: Set the vision for our support platform and AI with the Head of CSS, and turn it into a roadmap, a business case and results. Lead, coach and grow your team, and bring specialists and engineers together around one backlog and clear quarterly outcomes. Own how well our chatbot, Zendesk AI agents and Copilot perform: define what a good AI answer is, measure it, and switch off what doesn't help customers. Improve routing, user identification and self-service entry points so customers get to the right answer faster. Spend real time with customers and support agents: read tickets, listen to chats, see where people get stuck. Build a written case for every bigger piece of work, own the cost to serve, and check results against your forecast. Turn what you learn in support into evidence that helps product teams fix problems at the source. Your first months After 3 months: your team works from one backlog and one outcome roadmap, and the quality bar for AI answers is agreed. After 6 months: you've delivered and reported your first quarterly outcome, including how AI resolution compares with your forecast. What you bring to the table 5+ years as a Product Owner or Product Manager, ideally including support, CX, service or internal platform products. You've shipped AI or chatbot features in production and can name the metric you moved, the baseline and the result. You explain product decisions in commercial terms: cost, savings, effect, and what you learned when a forecast was wrong. You've managed people and led people who didn't report to you, ideally across departments. You do your own analysis with SQL or BI too

jobs.description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. jobs.title: Broker Development Manager
jobs.description: About Flock Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time. We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead. We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us! About the role Brokers bring in nearly all of Flock’s business, so they’re central to how we grow. As a Broker Development Manager, you’ll look after a panel of key broker partners with real growth potential, deepen the relationships we already have and build new ones as we move into new sectors. You’ll report to our Head of Distribution. You’ll show brokers what our connected fleet proposition does for their clients: it cuts risk and cost and keeps drivers safer. We’re AI-first, so you’ll use AI every day to research brokers, prepare for meetings and spot opportunities across your panel, leaving more time for the conversations that win business. What you’ll be doing Be the main face of Flock for a panel of key broker partners and grow the business you do together. Drive a high volume of quality submissions from your panel. Grow the panel, onboarding new brokers quickly and getting them trading. Find new ways to promote Flock’s appetite and proposition as we expand into new sectors. Build data-led growth plans for each account and follow them through. Support day-to-day trading so brokers win and keep business with Flock, keeping conversion and retention high. Work with underwriting, product and other teams across Flock towards shared growth goals. Use AI daily for broker research, meeting prep and pipeline analysis. What you’ll need At least five years managing broker relationships in insurance, with a strong reputation in the market. An existing network of broker contacts you can bring to Flock from day one. A strong understanding of the commercial broker market, competing carriers and how broker businesses work. A track record of beating revenue targets and working well with teams across a business. A consultative sales approach that matches Flock’s proposition to what each broker needs. Pace and energy: you move fast, spot opportunities and solve problems. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction . Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people , making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone. THE TEAM • ~160 people , around half in engineering, product and data • 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research • Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle • An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking , tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation The Opportunity Some of our biggest accounts are Chinese platforms, 3PLs and brokers moving millions of parcels into the UK. They grow with us when parcels arrive on time, issues get fixed fast, and someone on our side always knows exactly what’s going on. That someone is you. As our Mandarin-speaking Senior Operations Account Manager, you’ll take on some of the most complex of these accounts and set the standard for how we run account operations as we scale. Your mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure operations are never the reason a client hesitates to grow. Why This Role A team behind every client. To support this growth, we're moving from fractional legal support to our first full-time in-house lawyer. As we grow and our product and client base expand, we need someone who can own the legal function day to day. As this is our first full-time legal hire, we're looking for a self-starter who is passionate about the role and who will build, own and manage our internal legal function, creating value and protecting the business from risk. You’ll work autonomously and efficiently, leading on legal matters and bringing in external counsel where required, and you’ll report directly to our CFO. How you'll make a difference Take ownership of the legal function, including a smooth handover from the current fractional counsel. Lead on B2B SaaS contracting: draft, negotiate and manage customer, partner and supplier agreements, and maintain contract templates and playbooks. Update terms and conditions as new product features are released, working closely with product, sales and commercial colleagues. Act as product counsel on AI-enabled features: advise product and engineering on the legal and regulatory implications of AI in Street Group’s products (including data use and training, IP and output ownership, accuracy and liability, and transparency), and ensure customer terms, data terms and product documentation reflect them. Manage relationships with external law firms, including specialist advisers retained for equity and other matters, to ensure cost-effective use of external spend. Advise the executive team and, as required, the Board on legal, regulatory and risk matters. Keep up to date with legislative and regulatory change affecting the business. You have strong experience drafting and negotiating B2B SaaS agreements, ideally with institutional or regulated customers. You’re commercially focused: you act as a partner to sales, product and senior leadership and balance legal risk with commercial objectives. You have a sound understanding of data protection law and practical exposure to information security and technology risk. You have up-to-date knowledge of AI regulation and market practice as it affects SaaS products, with experience of advising on, or contracting around, AI features and of how customers and regulators are approaching them. jobs.description: About Lendable Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start: One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK Profitable since 2017 Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot ) So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days. We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. Join us if you want to Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1 Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting About the Role Lendable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident. You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them. AI is used widely across the business, in how we build software, run operations and serve customers, and that changes both what security incidents look like and how quickly we can respond to them. You will use AI and automation as a normal part of your work, and you will be able to investigate and respond to incidents where AI tooling is the cause, the target or the route in. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone with hands-on SOC experience and a track record of commanding incidents. What You’ll Be Doing 1. Alert Triage & Monitoring Triage and investigate alerts across our SIEM, EDR, identity and cloud tooling, taking escalations from our MSSP’s first-line team. Reduce false positives and alert fatigue by tuning detection rules, thresholds and suppressions. Utilise AI and automation to speed up triage, enrichment and response, and to remove repetitive manual work from the analyst workflow. 2. Incident Command & Response Command security incidents, coordinating technical response, decision-making and communications across Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders. Give clear, timely updates to executives during live incidents. Lead or support technical investigation and containment across endpoint, identity and cloud (AWS/GCP) environments, including incidents involving AI use, such as prompt injection, or credentials exposed through AI-generated code. Run blameless post-incident reviews, track actions to closure, and feed lessons back into detection, playbooks and controls. Take part in the out-of-hours on-call rota. 3. Operational Reporting & Assurance Track and report SecOps metrics that reflect reality, such as alert quality, time to triage, time to contain, incident volumes and root causes. jobs.title: Dex - Staff Product Engineer
jobs.description: Our Mission Human time and effort is the rarest thing in the universe. The fact that so many people hate what they do for work is a disaster on so many levels. How many people live quiet lives of misery? How many generational talents do we miss due to circumstance? Dex’s mission is to close the gap between Talent & Opportunity, we believe that work, and being productive, is part of the human condition, that regardless of AI, human passion, ingenuity and a desire to do things means that work will always exist. We are building Dex to create a future where technology helps every individual to understand their strengths, interests and unique abilities, and to connect with opportunities where they can thrive, because more people doing things they love leads to a better, happier and more productive world. We are starting by connecting the world's most ambitious software engineers with the companies that deserve them. The Role This is a Staff-level full-stack product role with a backend-heavy centre of gravity. You'll own complete product slices end-to-end — things like a candidate database with rich search and filtering, a dashboard that surfaces call transcripts and match history for our Talent Operations team, and the workflows that let them stack-rank candidates against a new role in minutes rather than hours. You ship these without needing to be guided step by step. You're not a specialist who hands off at the API boundary. You think in user outcomes and delivery units, and you're reliable: your code handles edge cases, your APIs have clean contracts, and the work you ship stays shipped. What You'll Do Own product delivery — take features from spec to production, backend-first but covering frontend and integration where needed Build and maintain backend systems — product APIs, data pipelines, and core infrastructure on our Python/FastAPI/Postgres stack Build with LLMs and agents — ship product features with significant LLM integration; contribute to the voice agent backend and information extraction systems Work across the stack — ship workable React/TypeScript frontend for product features; not a frontend specialist, but comfortable and pragmatic Collaborate with product and design — translate ambiguous requirements into concrete shipped work; In joining us, you will be helping to create cutting-edge technologies that will improve how we diagnose and treat brain disorders, ultimately improving and saving the lives of patients across the world. The Role: As Director of Quality Assurance, you will lead our Quality function across three core areas: the quality management system, design quality assurance including software quality assurance, and supplier quality assurance including QC activities. As we approach on-market release, you will also prepare the QMS for customer facing activities including post-market surveillance and complaint handling. You will work as a direct partner to our engineering teams and alongside our dedicated Regulatory Affairs leadership. Regulatory is not part of this role, but a function you will collaborate closely with. At CoMind, all team members work at least 4 days per week from our new Kings Cross offices, plus a flexible work-from-home day. Responsibilities: Team Leadership: Lead and develop our existing Quality team, instilling and maintaining a high performance culture. Ensure the CoMind QMS complies with the FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820, harmonised with ISO 13485) and 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records and signatures, while remaining customer focused and aligned with business needs. Audit Leadership: Lead our annual ISO 13485 certification audit, FDA inspection readiness and own the internal, supplier, and customer audit programmes. Cybersecurity: Provide oversight and guidance on cybersecurity aspects impacting product and business processes, including FDA's premarket cybersecurity guidance (Section 524B) Supplier & Manufacturing Quality: Lead supplier qualification, supplier audits, and manufacturing quality as we build toward commercial production. Work with suppliers to ensure effective Quality Assurance and Quality Control processes are implemented. Establish processes for maintaining Device Master Records, and transfer of batch records to CoMind. Post-Market Quality: Create the post-market side of the QMS from the ground up as we launch, including complaint handling, product analytics, and on-market quality processes Work with the RA function to compile Periodic Safety Update Reports (PSUR), vigilance reporting / MDR reporting, or field corrective actions/recalls in line with EU MDR/FDA obligations. Provide oversight and guidance on clinical evaluation / clinical data quality. Established SMEs are the backbone of local communities - representing over a third of our economy - yet have been largely neglected both by traditional high street banks and modern fintech providers. You will get an opportunity to work with different teams across the business including product squads, distribution, engineers and operations to deliver on Allica’s mission of becoming the UK’s most recommended business bank. We are rare amongst banks in that our senior leadership team have backgrounds at worldleading fintechs, which shows in their active engagement in both the strategic and execution elements of our rapidly scaling organisation. Because we are working on one of the last untapped fintech opportunities, in a new team it will mean that we're often working on entirely new challenges and unpicking complexity as we move along. No two days are ever the same. Role Description The Performance Marketing Manager at Allica Bank is responsible for scaling customer growth across our Business Bank Account and Lending products while maintaining an efficient CAC:LTV. This role combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution. Working closely with the team,you’ll bring strong analytical rigour, marketing instinct, and a bias for action - using data, automation, and AI to drive performance at scale. Principal Accountabilities Performance Marketing Execution & Strategy Lead hands-on campaign execution and strategy across Paid Social (with a focus on Meta Ads), Paid Search, PMax, and other key channels.  Optimise creative, user journeys, campaign structures, and targeting, with structured experiments & test-and-learn roadmaps to scale results efficiently.  Plan and deliver acquisition initiatives that balance near-term results with long-term growth goals. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence. Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology. AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen. About Frontier Faculty Frontier™ is a decision operating system. It puts AI to work on the decisions that matter most to large organisations, such as where to invest, how to allocate resources, and when to act. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Over months they connect it into a wider decision network, and over years they build an adaptive enterprise. Frontier is built by Faculty, an AI company that has delivered more than 400 systems since 2014 and is now part of Accenture. About Design at Frontier We’re a small team, growing deliberately - we’d rather have five designers who trust each other than fifteen who don't. We're tightly integrated with engineering. We prototype in code. We co-own the design system with developers. We're actively exploring what agentic-augmented design work looks like in practice, not in think pieces — and we're honest when we don't have the answer yet. We’re active in shaping the product culture at Frontier; putting people first, raising the quality bar and ensuring a coherent experience. You’ll be part of shaping that culture. About the role You'll be one of the most senior designers on Frontier, shaping a product that's still early enough that the decisions you make will define how it works for years. Day to day, you'll be designing the surfaces where people and agents collaborate on real clinical decisions — how evidence gets surfaced, how recommendations get explained, how humans push back, how teams learn. This is hard, unsolved design work. The existing patterns for AI interfaces mostly come from consumer chat products; they don't transfer cleanly to environments where the cost of a bad decision is measured in years of research or patient outcomes. You'll be expected to work end-to-end: from framing the problem with product and engineering, through prototyping in code and design canvases, through shipping. You'll help set the craft bar for the team, mentor the designers around you, and push back when something isn't good enough yet. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.   The IT Studio exists to remove the friction of work, unblocking Spotifiers anywhere, anytime, with simplicity and safety. We are the team behind the technology that approximately 8,000 Spotifiers rely on every day, spanning endpoint and device management, identity and access, networking and connectivity, IT service management and support, audio visual and meeting room technology, productivity and collaboration platforms, work management tooling, and the AI tools changing how everyone at Spotify works. Across 9 teams, we touch almost every part of how Spotify functions as a company.   We’re looking for an experienced engineering leader to lead a group of Engineering Managers and approximately 50 engineers and technicians across the studio. You’ll set engineering strategy, strengthen the technical practices that help our teams operate at their best, and partner closely with product and studio leadership to balance engineering investment with business priorities. Set and communicate engineering strategy across the studio, ensuring teams have clear technical direction aligned with IT’s mandate and Spotify’s business needs. Strengthen technical judgment across the Engineering Manager group, challenging processes that no longer add value and creating more space for architecture, quality, and team capability. Identify patterns and opportunities across teams and drive improvements in engineering practice, operational health, reliability, and ways of working. Establish and evolve engineering best practices across the studio, helping teams share knowledge and consistently improve how we build and operate technology. Champion reliability, security, compliance, and privacy as fundamental parts of engineering decision-making. Shape how AI is used across the company, both through the tools our squads build and how our engineers work day to day. Partner with studio and alliance leadership, procurement, legal, engineering counterparts, and teams across Spotify to make thoughtful technical investments and solve meaningful business problems. Who You Are You have 8+ years of engineering experience and experience leading Engineering Managers across multiple teams. You have led engineering organisations at scale and can demonstrate how the technical strategies you’ve shaped have influenced meaningful outcomes. jobs.title: Senior Applied Research Scientist - Personalization
jobs.description: The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them. Within Personalization, the Speak Team owns the development of Spotify's state-of-the-art speech models, contributing to speech recognition, speech synthesis, and speech-to-speech models. We craft voice models that match human-level emotional expressiveness, so we can deeply engage our listeners and support creators at scale. Our groundbreaking work on speech synthesis relies on state-of-the-art deep learning methods and evaluation techniques, highly efficient data processing and model serving, and capturing audio of outstanding quality from our voice talent pool. We're looking for a senior applied research scientist with experience in developing novel ML techniques and architectures and with a strong interest in working across a full production pipeline to produce state-of-the-art generative conversational speech-to-speech models. You'll collaborate with our engineering teams to help develop our production pipelines, explore new ideas and methods to improve quality, understanding and realism, as well as push the frontiers of what is possible with our speech technology. What You'll Do Develop and experiment with new methods for speech synthesis and speech recognition, along with end-to-end approaches, building on the latest research and ideas. Work towards the expansion of our speech use-cases targeting different markets and products. Be part of a highly motivated research team dedicated to building and creating models at scale to power the Spotify platform. Champion best practices for research and development, sharing your knowledge and experience with other researchers within Speak. Collaborate with our engineering and data teams on ideas requiring new infrastructure or new high-quality data, as well as to help improve our speech recognition and speech synthesis pipelines, and help turn proven ideas into scalable products. Who You Are You have a strong background in ML (PhD degree on top of professional experience), and experience in working with any of the following: transformers, GANs, diffusion models, flow matching, VAEs, audio codecs. You have experience in developing generative models for speech synthesis, speech recognition, audio/music, natural language processing, or computer vision. You have strong experience with Python, particularly PyTorch. You have strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical ideas with clarity to technical and non-technical people alike. You have experience in an academic or professional setting conducting high-quality research. Where You'll Be This role is based in London or Stockholm. We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.   At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more. The Role We're looking for an Information Security Engineer who can think broadly about how infrastructure is built, attacked, defended, and improved. You may have deep experience in one area—such as endpoint security, Active Directory, Data Loss Prevention, cloud security, identity, or detection and response—but you’re motivated by solving security problems across the environment. As an Information Security Engineer focused on infrastructure security, you'll help protect Palantir's global endpoints, servers, identity systems, applications, networks, and data flows. You'll work across teams to reduce attack surface, improve defensive controls, investigate security events, and turn security findings into durable architectural and operational improvements. This is not just a corporate security role; the adversaries we face are sophisticated. We need someone who understands both the details and the broader system: how a weakness in one part of the environment can create risk somewhere else, how controls interact, and how to build security improvements that hold up in practice. Core Responsibilities Design, implement, and improve security controls across endpoints, servers, identity systems, cloud services, SaaS applications, networks, and data flows. Assess security risks in new platforms, products, architectures, vendors, and services, and turn findings into practical recommendations and engineering work. Build and maintain automation for security operations, including configuration validation, drift monitoring, patching, access reviews, policy enforcement, alert triage, and security hygiene. Partner with Identity, Infrastructure, Engineering, Legal, and other Information Security teams to strengthen security architecture and address recurring risks. Turn insights from assessments, red team exercises, incident investigations, and operational reviews into durable fixes, such as configuration changes, architectural improvements, policy updates, and automation. Familiarity with common infrastructure attack paths, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures, and the controls used to prevent, detect, and contain them. This is a remote role that can be based anywhere in the UK.   This is a full selling role that will include prospecting, qualifying, managing, and closing new sales. In this role as an Account Executive, you will be responsible for selling the Everbridge Critical Event Managed (CEM) Platform into net new and existing customer base in public and private sectors. What you'll do: Develop a strong understanding of target buyers, domain knowledge, products and competitors. Prospect and identify new opportunities to build and maintain a healthy pipeline. Demonstrated ability to identify and sell to multiple buyers within an organization. Implement a consultative, solution selling, methodology. Work with Marketing, Business Development and Sales Team to execute campaigns to top buyers. Exceed assigned sales objectives and quarterly bookings quotas. Accurately manage and forecast your business using SF.com . What you'll bring: Minimum 5 years of sales experience with SaaS or hosted software to commercial accounts. Experience selling into larger commercial accounts. Experience selling: Major incident management, Cyber Security Operations, Infrastructure Operations, DevOps or Customer Support Operations Background or training in a consultative/Solution Sales process Solid blueprinting, consulting, and solution mapping skills Proven, measurable, and successful experience as a "hunter" Must have a verifiable history of meeting or exceeding quotas Experience using Salesforce a plus Experience with MEDDIC, Sandler Selling, SPIN Selling, or Solution Selling a plus.   #LI-HG1   About Everbridge   Everbridge empowers enterprises and government organizations to anticipate, mitigate, respond to, and recover stronger from critical events. In today’s unpredictable world, resilient organizations minimize impact to people and operations, absorb stress, and return to productivity faster when deploying critical event management (CEM) technology. Everbridge digitizes organizational resilience by combining intelligent automation with the industry’s most comprehensive risk data to Keep People Safe and Organizations Running™. For more information, visit  www.everbridge.com , read the company blog, and follow on Twitter. Everbridge… Empowering Resilience   Everbridge is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified Applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, or sex including sexual orientation and gender identity, national origin, disability, protected Veteran Status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.   Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

jobs.title: Chief Growth Officer
jobs.description: About Numan    Founded in 2018, we’ve already grown to be a 300+ team distributed across the globe, united by a singular mission: empowering people to take control of their health.   Numan is transforming health: we’ve built a cutting-edge platform that integrates diagnostics, medication, supplements, digital programmes, and doctor consultations. Giving people the tools they need to maximise life.   To deliver on our transformative mission, we are guided by our 5 company values:    • Patients first. • Learn fast. • Own the quality. • Succeed together. • Care deeply.   Backed by top-tier investors, Numan is already having a positive impact on hundreds of thousands of patients here in the UK, and we want you to help us deliver this mission! The Role:  This is a new role at Numan. It marks a significant intent in how we want to operate and invest in areas that make a meaningful impact to business performance. This role will report directly to our Founder & CEO and serve as a trusted advisor and partner to our Board, Executive team, and cross-functional leaders across Product, Commercial, and Growth Marketing. As an established D2C Growth leader, you will be a big influencer on our growth culture more broadly.  You'll be: Leading the company’s growth mission, acting as a trusted board advisor to investors and board members, clearly articulating Numan’s growth strategy, cohort dynamics, strategic bets, and capital allocation. Coaching and developing growth marketing leadership teams while raising execution pace, energy, and commercial ambition across the entire business. Formulating growth hypotheses and balancing macro market shifts with unit economics like CAC, LTV, and payback periods to validate and de-risk high-stakes investments. Rapidly diagnosing growth bottlenecks and building high-velocity multi-channel engines, focused on compounding growth. Serving as a culture beacon across the organisation to inspire and align teams that directly or indirectly impact revenue opportunities and growth levers. Monitoring full-funnel performance metrics daily to extract maximum leverage from lean budgets, scaling winning channels rapidly and pivoting decisively before returns diminish. Pioneering data and AI-driven growth across creative production, rapid experimentation, and advanced measurement. You'll have: Significant experience in building consumer businesses, either as a founder, operator holding roles directly responsible for growth. Proven track record scaling consumer businesses through major revenue step-changes (£10–100m, or £100m–250m+) navigating high-growth environments. Significant exposure to building toward substantial enterprise value creation in a growth or GTM role. Hands-on experience building new channels from scratch and navigating real operational battles, strategic pivots, and market headwinds. Experience shaping company growth strategy at the board level alongside founders and executive teams. A formidable combination of deep data analytics, performance marketing, and cutting-edge tools, balancing a strategic macro view with an extreme focus on execution. You have a strong bias for action and not just theory.  Total comfort navigating ambiguity and shifting markets, with a practical, analytical approach to making decisions and managing lean resources. jobs.title: Research Scientist – Foundation Models and Multimodal AI
jobs.description: About us Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed. Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity. K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners. Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK, Germany. Please submit your CV in English About the role: We are seeking a driven Research Scientist with hands-on expertise in Foundation Models (FMs) and Multimodal AI to help drive the next phase of our machine learning platform. In this role, you will bridge cutting-edge AI research and practical application. Rather than training massive base models from scratch, your focus will be on fine-tuning, adapting, and aligning open-weights foundation models across diverse data modalities (e.g. structured tabular data, single-cell scRNA-seq, image representations, and natural language) to build multimodal systems. In particular, you will be responsible for: Model adaptation and optimization: Adapt, fine-tune, and evaluate state-of-the-art open-source foundation models (e.g., domain-specific transformers, vision-language models) using fine-tuning and transfer learning strategies. Multimodal integration: Design and implement cross-modal alignment architectures (e.g., contrastive learning, projection heads, unified embedding spaces) to fuse structured, sequential, and text/image data layers. Pipeline and evaluation engineering: Build rigorous, domain-tailored benchmarking frameworks and evaluation pipelines to validate model reliability, generalization, and downstream task performance. jobs.title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-doctoral researcher (12 months) Mathematics of energy-efficient AI: diffusion models on emerging hardware
jobs.description: The question Generating one image with a diffusion model means evaluating a large neural network tens to hundreds of times. That repetition is where the energy goes, and it is part of why data-centre demand is now visible at grid scale: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory puts US data-centre electricity use at 176 TWh in 2023, 4.4 % of national consumption, a figure that more than doubled since 2017 largely because of AI servers, and projects 325–580 TWh by 2028. Emerging hardware attacks exactly this primitive: analog in-memory computing, silicon photonics, ferroelectric devices and stochastic computing perform the underlying matrix–vector products at lower energy than digital CMOS, under conditions on scale and precision, but return a perturbed result. The usual objection is that nobody can say in advance how much perturbation a model tolerates. In EMMA, this opportunity is pursued through a PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine as the primary demonstrator, complemented where appropriate by FeFET-based analog computing, so that device-level non-idealities are treated as explicit design parameters rather than as after-the-fact implementation losses. Diffusion models are an unusual case in which that question has a mathematical answer: their convergence theory bounds the discrepancy between the generated and target distributions by three terms, of which only one, the L 2 error of the learned score, depends on the hardware. That side is now in good shape: for stochastic samplers, bounds linear in the dimension under minimal assumptions on the data; for deterministic samplers, a matching theory under regularity. What is missing is the bridge. The theory is parameterised by a score error, the hardware literature by conductance noise, effective number of bits and photons per multiply–accumulate; nobody has written the map between them, in either direction. The quantisation literature for diffusion models reports image-quality scores; the induced L 2 score error, in the form the convergence theory needs, is directly measurable and goes unreported. One open sub-question sets the direction: the distinction between an error redrawn at each evaluation, as in stochastic computing, and an error frozen at write time, as in deterministic quantisation, has been settled in one setting only, and not the one hardware lives in; carrying it over is what this position exists to do. The work is judged on one concrete outcome. For at least one architecture, we want to show that theenergy gain from moving the score evaluation off digital CMOS is real, measured where it survives integration and not extrapolated from a single tile, and that it is paid for by a loss in sample quality that is small and, above all, tunable: a knob the designer sets, whose position the theory predicts rather than discovers afterwards. What you will do The work is organised in four packages, summarised below; the full research programme is available from the supervisors on request. 1. Make the score error measurable, starting from Gaussian targets where the whole error decomposition is closed-form. You will report the induced score error for a given perturbation of the network’s arithmetic, the number the theory needs and the quantisation literature does not report. 2. Map device physics onto the theory. Propagate the published error models for the technologies INL works on through the score network into an explicit score-error budget, separating what is proved from what is measured. 3. Extend the guarantees. Existing bounds assume a deterministic oracle, or a benign randomised one; extend them to error that is part frozen at write time and part redrawn at each call, and settle, on the way, which process the score error should be controlled along. 4. Co-design with INL, and deliver the proof of concept. Turn the score-error budget into an energy– accuracy frontier for INL’s PCM-based photonic matrix–vector engine, using device-calibrated circuitlevel models; a FeFE

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. The opportunity Our engineering teams build a product that enterprises run their purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash processes on every day. Much of the product knowledge behind it sits with our founders and domain experts. As we grow, we are moving from a project-oriented model, where features come top-down and success is measured by output, to a product-oriented one: empowered teams that own problems end-to-end and are measured by their impact on customers and the business. As Head of Product, you lead that shift. You build the product management practice for the BLP Platform from an early stage. Our first product managers are joining stream-aligned teams, starting with Invoice and Procurement, and the team will grow to 4–5 PMs as we expand. You hire them, coach them, and set the standard for what great product work looks like at BLP. You report to the CTO and work closely with Engineering, Projects, Sales, and our founders. What you’ll do Build and lead the product management practice for the BLP Platform: hire, coach, and develop a team of product managers as we scale. Move the product organization from an output-driven model to an outcome-driven one. Establish the product management craft at BLP: discovery practices, evidence-based decision making, and a clear standard for what “good” looks like in the role. Transfer product knowledge out of the experts’ heads and into the teams, without losing the domain depth that got us here. Build the direct line between our teams and our customers. Make our data usable for product decisions. We have BigQuery, PostHog, and prediction-rate analytics available, and we want product managers who reach for them by default. Shape how the product organization works as we grow: intake, prioritization, roadmapping, and the operating rhythm. Contribute directly to product strategy for the platform. What you bring 10+ years in product management, including experience leading or formally coaching product managers, with a real point of view on how product people are developed. Experience working in an empowered product model, where teams were assigned problems to solve rather than features to build. A track record of shipping enterprise B2B software that customers actually adopted. Experience moving an organization toward an empowered product model, including the political and cultural side of it. jobs.description: Functie  Reliability engineer   Beschrijving functie   De reliability engineer is een productie specialist die de totale levensduur van installatie bestudeert en analyseert hoe het bedrijf omgaat met investeringen en onderhoud van assets.  De reliability engineer is de expert in het identificeren van potentiële risico’s en het voorkomen van stilstanden. Daar problemen moeilijk volledig te voorkomen zijn, geeft de reliability engineer adviezen hoe te handelen bij storingen die plaatsvinden. Het doel is te voorkomen dat fouten in productiesystemen optreden.   De reliability engineer analyseert tevens de veiligheidsrisico’s geassocieerd met installatie fouten. Ter voorkoming van stilstand maakt de reliability engineer onderhoudsschema’s en analyseert statistische gegevens die helpen te voorspellen wanneer en hoe fouten voor kunnen komen. De reliability engineer ontwikkelt inspectie criteria die gebruikt worden om de asset health te monitoren.  Om dit te kunnen bereiken maakt de reliability engineer gebruik van een aantal technieken.   Voorlopige gevaren analyse: Preliminary hazard analysis is de initiële identificatie van potentiële gevaren en fouten in een productie proces of systeem Failure modes and effect analysis ( FMEA): Betreft het opsommen van de manieren dat een proces of systeem kan falen en wat de consequenties hiervan zijn. Criticality analysis: bepaalt hoe ernstig de consequenties zijn van een asset fout voor het productiesysteem van het bedrijf. Onderhoudbaarheid: gedetailleerde informatie hoe efficiënt en betrouwbaar het bedrijf een onderdeel kan repareren. Seeing the importance of our products for our customers, we recognize the need to continuously keep these secure in the ever evolving, fast-paced world. The security requirements in our landscape span four different areas:  Physical/embedded device security.  OT (operational technology) network security.  OT network to Priva-hosted cloud services communications.  Priva's hybrid on-prem/multi-cloud platform applications security, including applications, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines.   What makes this role truly unique is that our products contain long-lived hardware components that our customers run for years. jobs.title: Stagecoördinator – Passenger Services
jobs.description: Over dnata dnata is more than a global air and travel services provider. We connect people with possibilities and opportunities across 130+ airports in 34 countries through ground handling, cargo, travel, and catering & retail services. Our purpose is clear: to deliver on the promises our customers make. Our core values fuel everything we do: we are safe, we play to win, we respect everyone and work together as a team, and we are future thinking. At dnata, we foster diversity, nurture ambition, and celebrate achievement. If you're inspired by purpose and motivated to be part of a global team shaping the future of aviation and travel, we’d love to have you onboard. Als Stagecoördinator bij dnata Passenger Services speel jij een belangrijke rol in het creëren van een leerzame, veilige en succesvolle stageperiode. Je vormt de verbindende schakel tussen stagiairs, onderwijsinstellingen, recruitment en de operationele leidinggevenden. Daarbij kijk je verder dan alleen de stageperiode: je signaleert talent en helpt geschikte stagiairs hun weg te vinden naar een mogelijke functie binnen dnata. Zo draag je niet alleen bij aan de ontwikkeling van jonge professionals, maar ook aan de toekomstige personeelsbezetting en talentontwikkeling van Passenger Services! Monitoring en verbetering: Je houdt gegevens bij over instroom, lopende stages, afronding, uitval en doorstroom. Je rapporteert over de voortgang en begeleidingscapaciteit, signaleert knelpunten en doet voorstellen om het stageproces continu te verbeteren. Wat breng je mee? Vereisten: Mbo 4 werk- en denkniveau. Een relevante opleiding, bijvoorbeeld in luchtvaartdienstverlening, personeelsmanagement of begeleiding en coaching. jobs.title: Product Owner Werkplek & Support (Detachering / ZZP)
jobs.description: Hoe zorg je ervoor dat ruim 3.300 collega’s iedere dag goed hun werk kunnen doen? Als Product Owner Werkplek & Support geef je richting aan onze werkplekdienstverlening: van Microsoft 365 en randapparatuur tot support en servicedesk. Je bepaalt de roadmap, brengt focus aan en zorgt samen met het team en onze leveranciers dat we sneller, voorspelbaarder en met een betere gebruikerservaring leveren.  Wie ben jij Je bent iemand die verder kijkt dan de eerstvolgende sprint. Je kunt zelfstandig een visie en roadmap ontwikkelen, brengt focus aan en durft keuzes te maken wanneer belangen uiteenlopen.   Daarbij hoef je niet jarenlang de formele titel Product Owner te hebben gehad. We vinden het belangrijker dat je aantoonbaar eigenaarschap hebt genomen over een IT-product of -dienst en gewend bent om daarin richting en prioriteiten te bepalen. Je krijgt in deze rol veel ruimte. Je stelt zelf de roadmap op, maakt inhoudelijke keuzes en stuurt op verbeteringen binnen Werkplek & Support. Die autonomie betekent niet dat je alles alleen doet. Je stemt keuzes af het team, Servicemanager en teammanager zodat je elkaar kunt challengen op de juiste prioriteiten.   Het team bestaat uit collega's die al langere tijd bij Univé werken én collega's die relatief nieuw zijn. Het team heeft behoefte aan iemand die vanuit de Product Owner-rol richting en focus kan geven, zonder formeel leidinggevende te zijn.   Onze werkplek is sterk gebaseerd op Microsoft 365, maar omvat meer dan alleen de digitale werkplek. Denk ook aan randapparatuur, lokale ondersteuning en supportdienstverlening. Je hoeft niet zelf de technisch specialist te zijn. Wel begrijp je moderne werkplekdienstverlening voldoende om een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn voor engineers, architecten, securityspecialisten en leveranciers.   Een belangrijk onderdeel van je rol is de operationele samenwerking met onze externe servicedesk en andere leveranciers. Samen met het team geef je richting aan prioriteiten en verbeteringen en zorg je dat ontwikkelingen binnen Werkplek & Support goed aansluiten op de ondersteuning van onze medewerkers. Je voelt je daarnaast thuis in een omgeving die verandert. Je durft bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie te stellen, kunt omgaan met weerstand en neemt stakeholders mee wanneer nog niet alles vaststaat. Wat ga je doen Wat breng je mee? Voor ons is niet je exacte functietitel of het aantal jaren ervaring doorslaggevend. We willen vooral zien dat je dit soort verantwoordelijkheid eerder succesvol hebt gedragen. •    Je hebt aantoonbare ervaring met het bepalen van visie, roadmap en prioriteiten voor een IT-product of IT- dienst;    Je kunt verschillende belangen afwegen en duidelijke besluiten nemen en onderbouwen; •    Je kunt vanuit een Product Owner-rol richting en focus geven aan een team zonder formeel leidinggevende te zijn; •    Je bent sterk in stakeholder- en relatiemanagement en krijgt engineers, gebruikers, management en leveranciers mee; •    Je hebt ervaring met externe IT-dienstverleners en weet in operationele samenwerking, samen met het team, verbeteringen te realiseren; •    Je begrijpt werkplekdienstverlening en IT om inhoudelijk een stevige gesprekspartner te zijn; •    Je hebt ervaring met het verbeteren van dienstverlening en kunt sturen op snelheid, voorspelbaarheid en klantbeleving; •    Je kunt omgaan met weerstand, bestaande werkwijzen ter discussie stellen en koers houden wanneer nog niet alles duidelijk is; •    Je beschikt over hbo/wo-werk- en denkniveau. Ervaring met Microsoft 365 is welkom, maar diepgaande technische expertise is niet noodzakelijk. Ervaring met grotere transities of het insourcen van IT-dienstverlening is een pré. Als Product Owner Werkplek & Support ben je verantwoordelijk voor de visie, roadmap en priori

jobs.title: Integration Test Engineer
jobs.description: Role - Integration Test Engineer Company - iwell - Harmonizing Clean Energy Location - Utrecht About iwell At iwell, we are all about reinforcing energy security. We help European businesses become more energy independent. With growing regulations, extreme price volatility and rising grid issues, they need to be resilient. It is time to take charge and think ahead. We deliver energy management solutions that ensure that businesses are always in control of their energy. Our in-house developed EMS and modular battery storage drive profit through sustainability, making businesses future-proof.  We are a fast-growing international team of driven and collaborative talents, from engineers and software developers to creative thinkers and customer-focused business developers. No matter what your strong suit is, we always are looking for people who are determined to make a positive impact: iwell is committed to form a diverse and inclusive team to tackle the challenges of the energy transition.    The Role The proof is in the pudding, they say in the UK, however, we believe proof is in the test data. All our systems and their interactions within the larger energy ecosystem are thoroughly tested. We are serving a diverse customer base with strict demands, our services power business and key infrastructure. We demand that our products are subjected to a wide range of testing during the integration and development phase. You will work within the battery system team, where software and hardware come together in the products we develop for our customers.  We will rely on your experience, hands-on approach and judgment. Knowledge of technical standards and grid operator connection requirements. A mobile phone allowance of EUR 25 per month Additional activitie

jobs.title: Data Platform Engineer
jobs.description: About the role At ClickHouse, we believe in making product decisions grounded in data, not gut feelings. To support that, we've built a comprehensive internal data warehouse — read more about it on our blog . It powers analytics, forecasting, and decision-making across every team in the company. Our stack centers on ClickHouse as the core storage and processing engine, complemented by dbt , Airflow , S3 , AWS , Superset , and GitHub Actions . We ingest data from 30+ distinct external sources, process over 2.5 PB of data, and deliver most data marts to business consumers with a 1-hour end-to-end latency - a standard that demands highly optimized, rock-solid transformation pipelines. We're looking for a Senior Data Engineer to help evolve the DWH platform, push its technical boundaries, and deliver reliable, high-performance data models to business users across the organization. Key Responsibilities DWH Platform Development Design and develop reusable Airflow components - operators, connectors, and hooks - along with custom integrations tailored to our data architecture. Build reusable dbt macros and abstractions: incremental strategies, ETL building blocks, and generic data quality tests, all optimized for ClickHouse-specific behavior and our data patterns. Develop DataOps tooling - CI pipelines, data migration frameworks, and security controls - with a strong focus on reliability, self-service usability, and scale. Team contributions Conduct thorough code reviews for team members and other team contributors. Actively participate in technical and architectural design discussions. Drive technical leadership in specific areas of our stack. Continuously improve the team's development environment, with a focus on automation - including AI-assisted workflows. Contribute to platform stability through proactive troubleshooting and timely incident resolution. Data modeling Develop, refactor, and optimize business data models in line with our modeling standards and ClickHouse best practices. Mentor and support contributors through code reviews and technical guidance. Lead the design and implementation of the most technically demanding data marts - particularly those involving high data velocity, large volumes, or complex business logic. Qualifications Required: Exceptional SQL skills - this is non-negotiable. Strong hands-on experience with Airflow , dbt , and Python . Proven track record building and optimizing large-scale, high-throughput data pipelines. Solid understanding of data warehousing fundamentals: ETL/ELT, dimensional modeling, and data quality. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related field. Comfortable thriving in a fast-paced startup environment — exciting and dynamic, but sometimes wonderfully chaotic.
